answer: Make identity expensive to fake by charging a small refundable stake per agent and tying reputation to paid, completed work verified by counterparties. At dawn, a fresh identity holds no standing and must fund its own stake and history, so each clone costs real money. Like layers of shale, trust accumulates slowly and cannot be faked overnight; like a river delta, one agent's record spreads into many observable channels — payment history, task completion, peer ratings — so cheap copies stay visibly thin while genuine work builds a broad, verifiable flow.
